findings.claim: The bootstrap component page still describes configure_network.yml as only the firewall role on all hosts; it now also writes the DNS fallback drop-in on radxa and orange_pi_4a.

verdict.text: The change does what the plan asks.
One new play writes a NetworkManager global-DNS drop-in on radxa and orange_pi_4a, and a handler reloads it.
The play is idempotent, the reload command works on both NetworkManager versions, and the test checks the r2 contract.
One knowledge page that describes the playbook is now incomplete.
That is a plain docs fix, so the verdict is fix.
r4 cannot be judged until the operator applies the play.

Gates: I ran `loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree myself: "pass gate pre_commit, pass gate cli_tests, pass eval-row r1, r2, r3; stamp green: b462c4ab4b88e0c0c59463b4326f2ae4702455e54ca573981bfef30659d3678d".
The change is still uncommitted in the worktree, and the stamp covers that tree.
Code read in full: the new play in `bootstrap/playbooks/configure_network.yml`, `cli/tests/test_bootstrap_dns_fallback.py`, ADR 0033, and both node-page diffs.
Idempotence: `copy` with fixed content, owner and mode reports changed only when the file differs.
The handler's `changed_when: true` runs only when notified.
The play name's em dash follows the two firewall plays above it.
Nodes (read-only over SSH): radxa runs NM 1.46.0 and orange_pi_4a runs 1.36.6.
On both, `/etc/resolv.conf` is a regular file headed "Generated by NetworkManager" with `search home` and only `192.168.2.254`.
`nmcli general reload --help` lists both the `conf` and `dns-rc` flags on both nodes.
The man pages say config can be reloaded with SIGHUP or the D-Bus Reload call, and that the `*` global domain overrides the active connection's servers and domains.
Neither node has a conf.d file that clashes with `90-dns-fallback.conf`.
radxa's `/etc/NetworkManager/conf.d/10-dns-resolved.conf` is a comment-only file that masks the lib file's `dns=systemd-resolved`, so NM writes resolv.conf itself.
orange_pi_4a sets `dns=default` and `rc-manager=file`.
systemd-resolved is active on orange_pi_4a but does not own resolv.conf.
I could not read `NetworkManager-intern.conf` without root.
Whether reload alone rewrites the live file is still unverified, as the author says.
r4 will show it.
Timeout claim: with glibc, three servers, `timeout:1` and `attempts:2`, each try waits at least 1 s, so about 6 s worst case per name.
The ADR is right.
r1: syntax-check passes, and the row's command is exactly the check its fails_when names.
r2: the test finds the one play whose copy task writes the drop-in path.
It asserts the hosts equal exactly {radxa, orange_pi_4a}, the servers equal the ordered list, the options equal `timeout:1,attempts:2`, and `searches == home`.
A wrong host, order, option or missing search fails it, which matches fails_when.
r3: `kmctl check` passes.
r4 (judgment): cannot be judged.
The play has not been applied, so neither node's resolv.conf nor Bifrost's container shows the new servers yet.
It stays open until the operator runs the playbook and restarts Bifrost.
Consistency: `docs/reference/dns.md` and `docs/how-to/check-lab-dns.md` cover the public lab zone, not node resolvers, and stay true.
Fallback happens only on a timeout, so the rebind-filtering note still holds.
No docs/ change is needed.
`.okf/components/bootstrap.md` is stale (f1).
Rules: the play's header comment gives reasons and a trap (why these two hosts, why `searches=home`, the Podman restart), which minimal-comments allows.
The prose is plain, and the diff touches only what the ticket needs.
No checklist lines were printed for this round.
f1 (docs, non-blocking): `.okf/components/bootstrap.md` row 9 says `configure_network.yml` runs on "all" hosts with "role `firewall`: ufw default deny and the HashiStack ports".
The playbook now also writes the NetworkManager DNS fallback on radxa and orange_pi_4a.
Add that to the row, for example with a link to ADR 0033.
Then add the page to `sources`, or run `kmctl summary ack` if needed.
The live reload path (`nmcli general reload conf,dns-rc` rewriting resolv.conf without a NetworkManager restart) has not been tested.
If r4 shows the file unchanged after the run, `systemctl restart NetworkManager` applies the same file, as the plan's R1 says.
